# Control narrative template for pumps and on/off valves

## 0. Approach

The 90% that repeats is written once as a class narrative. Each tag then gets a short instance sheet that holds only its own data.

| Layer | Document | Contains | Owner | Changes by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Class narrative (CLS-PMP, CLS-VLV) | All behavior: states, transitions, sequences, interlocks, alarms, abnormal handling, operator interface, default setpoints | Controls lead | MOC, revision clouds, change log |
| 2 | Instance sheet (one per tag, generated from the tag database) | Class and revision, enabled features, tag links, setpoint values, interlock rows, open items | Integrator | Edit tag database, regenerate |
| 3 | Deviations (inside the instance sheet) | Requirements `FR-<tag>-NNN` that differ from the class | Integrator proposes, controls lead approves | MOC |

**Rules against drift**
1. The instance sheet contains no behavior prose. It states "Behavior: CLS-PMP rev X" and lists the requirement IDs that apply.
2. The integrator never copies class text into an instance. Generate the instance sheet from the tag database.
3. A deviation needs a justification. If three or more instances need the same deviation, promote it to a class option through MOC.
4. Each class requirement is tested once, at library FAT. Each tag gets a short instance checkout, generated from its sheet.
5. A class change goes through MOC. Query the tag database to list every affected instance.

**Test method codes:** T = class type test at library FAT (once per class revision). I = instance checkout (per tag). D = document inspection.

The class narratives cover the standard library only. Mixproof valves with seat lift and modulating valves need their own classes (OI-9). SIS functions are out of scope and belong in the SRS.

---

## A. Class narrative CLS-PMP, rev A (draft)

### A1. Purpose and boundaries
CLS-PMP controls one motor-driven pump. Variants are fixed speed (FIX) and variable speed with VFD (VFD). The suction protection and flow-path features are options. A parent module (unit, CIP circuit, or phase) sends the start request and, for VFD, the speed setpoint. The class contains no PID loop. A parent loop writes the speed setpoint.

### A2. Instance data fields
| Field | Meaning | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Tag, description, area | Identification | Yes |
| Variant | FIX or VFD | Yes |
| Drive tag, interface | VFD only | VFD |
| Run feedback source | Drive status or contactor auxiliary | Yes |
| Suction protection | Enabled or disabled, with PV tag | Yes |
| Flow-path proof | Enabled or disabled (parent signal) | Yes |
| Parent module | Module that sends requests | Yes |
| Setpoint values | `SP-<tag>-NN`, same IDs as A11 where overriding | Yes |
| Interlock rows | Extra cause/effect rows | If any |
| Deviations | `FR-<tag>-NNN` | If any |

### A3. Modes and states
Modes: **Auto** (the parent commands), **Manual** (the operator commands at the faceplate), **OOS** (out of service).

| State | Entry | Run command | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| OOS | Operator selects OOS from STOPPED or TRIPPED | Off | STOPPED |
| STOPPED | Reset, stop complete, or OOS cleared | Off | STARTING, OOS |
| STARTING | Accepted start request | On | RUNNING, STOPPING, TRIPPED |
| RUNNING | Run feedback confirmed | On | STOPPING, TRIPPED |
| STOPPING | Stop request | Off | STOPPED, TRIPPED |
| TRIPPED | Any trip cause | Off | STOPPED (by reset) |

### A4. Transitions
| ID | Transition | Condition | Initiator | Automation level | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-PMP-010 | STOPPED → STARTING | New start request and all permissives in A5 true | Parent (Auto) or operator (Manual) | Automatic in Auto, manual in Manual | T |
| FR-PMP-011 | STARTING → RUNNING | Start sequence A7 complete | Module | Automatic | T |
| FR-PMP-012 | STARTING or RUNNING → STOPPING | Stop request | Parent or operator | Same as FR-PMP-010 | T |
| FR-PMP-013 | STOPPING → STOPPED | Stop sequence A7 complete | Module | Automatic | T |
| FR-PMP-014 | Any active state → TRIPPED | Any cause in A6 | Module | Automatic | T |
| FR-PMP-015 | TRIPPED → STOPPED | Operator reset and all causes in A6 clear | Operator only | Manual | T |
| FR-PMP-016 | STOPPED or TRIPPED → OOS, and OOS → STOPPED | Operator selection | Operator | Manual | T |
| FR-PMP-017 | Start request edge rule | A start request must change from false to true. A request held true across a reset or a PLC restart does not start the pump. | Module | Automatic | T |
| FR-PMP-018 | Mode change | Auto ↔ Manual keeps the state and the last speed setpoint. A stop request from the new commanding source then applies. | Operator | Manual | T |

### A5. Start permissives
| ID | Permissive | When active | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-PMP-030 | No latched trip | Always | T |
| FR-PMP-031 | Minimum off time elapsed (SP-PMP-01) | Always | T |
| FR-PMP-032 | Drive ready | VFD | T |
| FR-PMP-033 | Suction PV quality good and above the suction OK value | Suction protection enabled | T, I |
| FR-PMP-034 | Flow path proven by the parent | Flow-path proof enabled | T, I |
| FR-PMP-035 | E-stop circuit healthy (hardwired status input) | Always | T, I |
| FR-PMP-036 | If any permissive is false, reject the request, stay STOPPED, and show the first false permissive on the faceplate | Always | T |

### A6. Interlocks (trip causes)
The project has no cause-and-effect chart, so the rows are written here. Every row removes the run command, enters TRIPPED, and is **latched**. The only reset is FR-PMP-049.

| ID | Cause | First-out text |
|---|---|---|
| FR-PMP-040 | Suction PV below the trip value for the dry-run delay. The check is masked during the start mask time after the run command. | DRY RUN |
| FR-PMP-041 | Suction PV quality bad (value outside the analog failure limits) while suction protection is enabled. Not masked. | SUCTION PV BAD |
| FR-PMP-042 | Drive fault (VFD) | DRIVE FAULT |
| FR-PMP-043 | Drive communication loss longer than SP-PMP-05 (VFD) | DRIVE COMMS |
| FR-PMP-044 | Fail to start: run feedback not confirmed within the start timeout | FAIL TO START |
| FR-PMP-045 | Fail to stop: run feedback still true when the stop timeout expires | FAIL TO STOP |
| FR-PMP-046 | Run feedback lost while the run command is on | RUN FB LOST |
| FR-PMP-047 | Flow-path proof lost for longer than SP-PMP-13 while STARTING or RUNNING | PATH LOST |
| FR-PMP-048 | E-stop circuit not healthy | E-STOP |
| FR-PMP-049 | Reset rule: only the operator resets. The reset is ignored while any cause is active. A valid reset also sends a fault reset to the drive. No cause resets automatically. | n/a |

All tests are T. Rows 040, 041, 043, and 044 also get I when the feature is enabled on the instance.

### A7. Sequences
**FR-PMP-060 Start**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check permissives A5 | All true | One scan | Reject request, stay STOPPED, show first false permissive |
| 2 | Write speed reference (VFD). Set run command. Start the dry-run mask timer. | Run feedback true | SP-PMP-02 | TRIPPED, FAIL TO START |
| 3 | Hold | Run feedback true for SP-PMP-03 | SP-PMP-02 (counted from step 2) | TRIPPED, FAIL TO START |

**FR-PMP-061 Stop**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Clear run command. The drive stops on its configured ramp (VFD). | Run feedback false for SP-PMP-03 | SP-PMP-04 | TRIPPED, FAIL TO STOP, alarm |

The stop timeout must be longer than the ramp-down time. Check this at instance checkout (I).

**FR-PMP-062 Trip** (test T)
1. Clear the run command in the same scan as the cause.
2. Latch the first-out cause.
3. Raise the alarm in A9.

The drive coasts to stop on a trip (OI-3).

### A8. Speed control (VFD only)
There is no PID in the class.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-PMP-050 | Auto: the speed reference is the parent setpoint, limited between minimum and maximum speed. | T |
| FR-PMP-051 | Manual: the speed reference is the operator entry, with the same limits. | T |
| FR-PMP-052 | The reference is 0–100 % of drive maximum speed. Ramp times are SP-PMP-14 and SP-PMP-15. The drive applies the ramps. | T, I |
| FR-PMP-053 | The speed deviation alarm in A9 shows when the speed feedback differs from the reference. The pump does not trip. | T |

### A9. Alarms
The project has no alarm database, so the alarms are listed here. Priorities are provisional (OI-8).

| ID | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| AL-PMP-01 | Trip active (first-out cause shown). One alarm per cause in A6. | See below | Find the cause. Reset. |
| AL-PMP-02 | Suction PV below pre-alarm value (suction protection enabled) | Medium | Check the suction source. |
| AL-PMP-03 | Speed deviation longer than SP-PMP-08 | Low | Check the drive and the process. |
| AL-PMP-04 | Run feedback true while no run command, longer than SP-PMP-06 | High | Stop the pump locally. Call maintenance. |
| AL-PMP-05 | Speed feedback quality bad | Low | Check the drive link. |

Provisional priorities for AL-PMP-01 are High for DRY RUN, E-STOP, and FAIL TO STOP, and Medium for all other causes. Test method for the table is T.

### A10. Abnormal handling
| ID | Event | Required behavior | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-PMP-070 | Analog input outside SP-PMP-09 to SP-PMP-10 | Set quality bad. The effect depends on the use, as in FR-PMP-041 and AL-PMP-05. | T |
| FR-PMP-071 | Drive comms loss | Trip as FR-PMP-043. The drive stops on its own when it loses the run command or the link within SP-PMP-05. | T, I |
| FR-PMP-072 | PLC power loss and restart | Run command off. State STOPPED. Mode is retained. Trips are not retained, because permissives are evaluated again. No automatic start (FR-PMP-017). | T |
| FR-PMP-073 | Drive power loss | Run feedback lost, so FR-PMP-046 applies. No automatic restart. | T |
| FR-PMP-074 | HMI communication loss | No effect on state, mode, or commands. | T |
| FR-PMP-075 | Fail position | The run command is energized to run. Loss of the output or the signal means stop. | T, I |

### A11. Class default setpoints
| ID | Description | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-PMP-01 | Minimum off time | 30 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-02 | Start timeout | 10 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-03 | Run feedback confirm time | 2 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-04 | Stop timeout | 30 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-05 | Drive comms loss time | 2 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-06 | Unexpected-run alarm delay | 5 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-07 | Speed deviation band | 5 | % | confirm |
| SP-PMP-08 | Speed deviation delay | 30 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-09 | Analog low failure limit | 3.6 | mA | standard value, confirm at loop check |
| SP-PMP-10 | Analog high failure limit | 21.0 | mA | standard value, confirm at loop check |
| SP-PMP-11 | Default minimum speed | 30 | % | confirm |
| SP-PMP-12 | Default maximum speed | 100 | % | confirm |
| SP-PMP-13 | Flow-path loss delay | 3 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-14 | Default ramp-up time | 10 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-15 | Default ramp-down time | 10 | s | confirm |

### A12. Operator interface
| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-PMP-090 | The faceplate shows mode, state, first-out cause, first false permissive, speed reference and feedback (VFD), and suction PV (if enabled). | I |
| FR-PMP-091 | Manual mode gives START, STOP, and speed entry. Auto mode gives none of these. | T |
| FR-PMP-092 | RESET and the mode selector are always available. OOS needs the supervisor privilege level. | T |
| FR-PMP-093 | Prompts are in the table below. Operations signs off on them (OI-7). | D |

| Prompt | Trigger | Text |
|---|---|---|
| PR-PMP-01 | Operator pushes RESET after any trip | "Find the cause of the trip. Then push RESET." |
| PR-PMP-02 | Operator pushes RESET after a DRY RUN trip | "WARNING: Do not reset until liquid is in the suction line. Dry running damages the pump seal." |

## B. Class narrative CLS-VLV, rev A (draft)

### B1. Purpose and boundaries
CLS-VLV controls one on/off valve with a spring return and one solenoid output. Variants are NC (spring closes) and NO (spring opens). Feedback options are open+closed, closed only, open only, or none. A parent module sends open and close requests. The command is logical ("open" or "close"). The output polarity follows the variant.

### B2. Instance data fields
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Tag, description, area, parent module | Identification |
| Variant | NC or NO |
| Feedback option | See B1 |
| Fault output | Rest position (default), open, or close |
| Travel time overrides | `SP-<tag>-NN` |
| Interlock rows | Rows in the A6 format |
| Deviations | `FR-<tag>-NNN` |

### B3. States
| State | Entry | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|
| OOS | Operator selection from CLOSED, OPEN, or FAULTED | CLOSED or OPEN (derived from feedback) |
| CLOSED | Closed feedback confirmed | OPENING, FAULTED, OOS |
| OPENING | Open command accepted | OPEN, FAULTED, CLOSING |
| OPEN | Open feedback confirmed | CLOSING, FAULTED, OOS |
| CLOSING | Close command or close interlock | CLOSED, FAULTED, OPENING |
| FAULTED | Travel timeout or discrepancy | Rest-position state, by reset |

Modes are Auto, Manual, and OOS, with the same rules as FR-PMP-018.

### B4. Transitions, interlocks, abnormal handling
| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-VLV-010 | CLOSED → OPENING: open command, no fault, and all open permissives in the instance interlock rows true. If a permissive is false, reject the command and show the reason. | T |
| FR-VLV-011 | OPENING → OPEN: open feedback true within SP-VLV-01. Without open feedback, the module assumes OPEN after SP-VLV-01 and raises no travel alarm. | T |
| FR-VLV-012 | OPEN → CLOSING: close command or a close interlock. CLOSING → CLOSED: closed feedback true within SP-VLV-02. | T |
| FR-VLV-013 | OPENING or CLOSING → FAULTED when the travel time expires. Raise AL-VLV-01 or AL-VLV-02. | T |
| FR-VLV-014 | OPEN or CLOSED → FAULTED when the feedback differs from the commanded position for SP-VLV-03, or when both feedbacks are true. Raise AL-VLV-03. | T |
| FR-VLV-015 | In FAULTED, move the output to the fault output position. After operator reset and with feedback showing the rest position, go to the rest-position state. | T |
| FR-VLV-016 | A close interlock row moves the valve to CLOSING in every mode, including Manual. A row marked latched holds the valve until operator reset. A row marked auto-reset lets the valve follow the command again when the cause clears. | T |
| FR-VLV-017 | PLC power loss, restart, air loss, or remote I/O loss: the output goes to the rest position (spring). On restart, the commands are cleared and the state follows the feedback. No fault is retained. No open command is remembered. | T, I |
| FR-VLV-018 | Operator interface: the faceplate shows mode, state, feedback, and interlock reason. OPEN and CLOSE are available in Manual only. RESET is always available. | T |

### B5. Sequences
| Sequence | Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open (FR-VLV-020) | 1 | Check permissives | All true | One scan | Reject, show reason |
| | 2 | Move output to the open position | Open feedback true | SP-VLV-01 | FAULTED, AL-VLV-01 |
| Close (FR-VLV-021) | 1 | Move output to the close position | Closed feedback true | SP-VLV-02 | FAULTED, AL-VLV-02 |

### B6. Alarms and default setpoints
| ID | Condition | Priority (confirm, OI-8) | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| AL-VLV-01 | Fail to open | Medium | Check air and the valve. |
| AL-VLV-02 | Fail to close | Medium | Check air and the valve. |
| AL-VLV-03 | Position discrepancy | Medium | Check the proximity switches and the valve. |
| EV-VLV-04 | Close interlock active (event, no alarm) | n/a | None. |

| ID | Description | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-VLV-01 | Open travel time | 5 | s | confirm; override for large valves |
| SP-VLV-02 | Close travel time | 5 | s | confirm; override for large valves |
| SP-VLV-03 | Discrepancy delay | 2 | s | confirm |

## C. Instance sheet: P-4021 (CIP supply pump)

**Behavior:** CLS-PMP rev A, variant VFD. Requirements FR-PMP-010 to FR-PMP-093 apply, with the features below. This instance has no deviations.

### C1. Instance data
| Field | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Tag, description, area | P-4021, CIP supply pump, CIP | Given |
| Variant | VFD | Given |
| Drive tag, interface | VFD-4021, fieldbus | confirm (OI-3) |
| Run feedback source | Drive status word | confirm (OI-3) |
| Suction protection | Enabled. PV is PT-4022 (suction pressure, bar g, range per instrument index). | PT-4022 as suction transmitter: confirm (OI-1) |
| Flow-path proof | Enabled. Signal comes from the parent CIP circuit module. | confirm (OI-4) |
| Parent module | CIP circuit module (tag per CIP module narrative) | confirm (OI-4) |
| Auto speed setpoint source | Parent CIP circuit module | confirm (OI-5) |
| Extra interlock rows | None | Given |
| Deviations | None | Given |

### C2. Instance setpoints
These are the only values the instance sheet adds. All other values come from A11.

| ID | Description | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-4021-01 | Suction trip value (PT-4022) | 0.3 | bar g | confirm |
| SP-4021-02 | Suction pre-alarm value | 0.45 | bar g | confirm |
| SP-4021-03 | Suction OK value (start permissive and trip clear) | 0.6 | bar g | confirm |
| SP-4021-04 | Dry-run trip delay | 3 | s | confirm |
| SP-4021-05 | Dry-run start mask time | 10 | s | confirm |
| SP-4021-06 | Minimum speed (overrides SP-PMP-11) | 35 | % | confirm |
| SP-4021-07 | Ramp-up time (overrides SP-PMP-14) | 15 | s | confirm |
| SP-4021-08 | Ramp-down time (overrides SP-PMP-15) | 15 | s | confirm |

Order rule: the trip value must be below the pre-alarm value, and the pre-alarm value below the suction OK value. The ramp-down time must be below the stop timeout. Check both at instance checkout.

### C3. Requirements enabled on this tag
| ID | Requirement | Enables | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-P4021-001 | Suction protection uses PT-4022 with SP-4021-01 to SP-4021-05. | FR-PMP-033, 040, 041, AL-PMP-02 | I |
| FR-P4021-002 | The flow-path signal from the parent is a start permissive and a trip cause. | FR-PMP-034, 047 | I |
| FR-P4021-003 | Speed limits and ramps use SP-4021-06 to SP-4021-08. The maximum is SP-PMP-12. | FR-PMP-050 to 052 | I |
| FR-P4021-004 | Drive stop on comms loss and on run-command loss is set in VFD-4021 to match SP-PMP-05. | FR-PMP-043, 071 | I |

### C4. Instance checkout (generated from C3 and the class)
| Check | Method | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| Start inhibit | Simulate PT-4022 below SP-4021-03. Request start. | Request rejected. Faceplate shows suction permissive. |
| Dry-run trip | Run the pump. Wait for SP-4021-05. Simulate PT-4022 below SP-4021-01 for longer than SP-4021-04. | Pump trips, DRY RUN latched. |
| Dry-run reset | Raise PT-4022 above SP-4021-03. Push RESET. Confirm the PR-PMP-02 prompt. | Pump goes to STOPPED. It does not restart. |
| Mask | Drop PT-4022 below SP-4021-01 during the start mask time only. | No trip. |
| PV bad | Force PT-4022 outside the analog failure limits. | Trip, SUCTION PV BAD, latched. |
| Drive comms | Remove the VFD-4021 link while running. | Trip, DRIVE COMMS. The drive stops. |
| Ramps | Start and stop. | Stop completes within the stop timeout. |
| Restart | Cycle PLC power while running. | Pump stops. No start on power-up. |

## E. Using the template on a project
1. Issue CLS-PMP and CLS-VLV once, at one revision, with operations sign-off.
2. Add each pump and valve as a tag-database row with the A2 or B2 fields.
3. Generate the instance sheets and the instance checkout lists from the tag database.
4. Review only the instance deviations and open items. Do not review class text again per tag.
5. After construction starts, change class text only through MOC. Update the instance data by tag-database change.

Assumptions to check: PT-4022 as a suction transmitter in bar g, the VFD fieldbus interface, and every setpoint marked "confirm". I made all of them to give you a complete example.
